newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to continue plan for Irish Connemara field.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to continue plan for Irish Connemara field.

text.p: Norway's state-owned oil company Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it would continue development plans for the Connemara oilfield offshore Ireland with work due to begin next spring.
Statoil previously intended to stage test production in the first half of 1997 before taking a development decision, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.

"The present decision means we are working as if a development go-ahead had been given, but allows us to break off if we gat any unpleasant surprises," said Jacob Sannes, exploration and development manager for Statoil's UK and Irish operations.
Connemara lies in 365 metres of water and is due to be developed with a production ship. If the project goes ahead it would be the first producing field offshore west of Ireland.
